served.stem: 2-Pentyne (drawn), an UNsymmetrical internal alkyne, is treated with H2O, HgSO4, and H2SO4. Which statement best describes the outcome?
choices: A carboxylic acid forms by oxidative cleavage of the triple bond
A single aldehyde forms, because Markovnikov addition of water to an internal alkyne always delivers the oxygen to a chain-end carbon of the molecule
A roughly equal mixture of two regioisomeric ketones (2-pentanone and 3-pentanone) forms, because neither alkyne carbon is strongly favored
No reaction occurs, because internal alkynes are unreactive toward Hg(II)/acid
Only 2-pentanone forms, because Markovnikov addition always places the carbonyl oxygen on C2, the alkyne carbon carrying the shorter alkyl chain
served.bankWhy: For an unsymmetrical INTERNAL alkyne, the two carbons of the triple bond are similar in substitution, so Markovnikov selectivity is poor and acid-catalyzed hydration gives a mixture of both possible ketones. Internal alkynes give ketones, never aldehydes; the reaction does occur; and no C-C cleavage happens under these conditions.

answer.text: A roughly equal mixture of two regioisomeric ketones (2-pentanone and 3-pentanone) forms, because neither alkyne carbon is strongly favored
answer.line: Each alkyne carbon carries one alkyl group, so water has no favorite end. Oxygen lands on C2 about as often as on C3: two ketones.

steps: Name the reaction. Water with HgSO4 and H2SO4 adds across the triple bond Markovnikov style, giving an enol that turns into a ketone.
Compare the two alkyne carbons. One carries a methyl, the other an ethyl: each has one alkyl group, so neither is clearly more substituted.
With no favorite, oxygen goes to C2 or C3 in about equal amounts: 2-pentanone and 3-pentanone.

choices.text: A carboxylic acid forms by oxidative cleavage of the triple bond
choices.note: Cleaving an alkyne to acids is what ozone or hot KMnO4 does. Mercury and acid only add water.

choices.text: A single aldehyde forms, because Markovnikov addition of water to an internal alkyne always delivers the oxygen to a chain-end carbon of the molecule
choices.note: An aldehyde comes from a terminal alkyne by hydroboration. An internal alkyne has no end carbon in the triple bond to put the oxygen on.

choices.text: A roughly equal mixture of two regioisomeric ketones (2-pentanone and 3-pentanone) forms, because neither alkyne carbon is strongly favored
choices.note: Two equally substituted carbons, two ketones in about equal amounts.

choices.text: No reaction occurs, because internal alkynes are unreactive toward Hg(II)/acid
choices.note: The textbook example is a terminal alkyne, which is where this idea comes from. Internal alkynes hydrate too.

choices.text: Only 2-pentanone forms, because Markovnikov addition always places the carbonyl oxygen on C2, the alkyne carbon carrying the shorter alkyl chain
choices.note: 2-Pentanone does form. But Markovnikov has nothing to choose between two equally substituted carbons, so 3-pentanone forms too.

student.lockIt: Alkyne hydration gives ketones; an internal alkyne with similar ends gives both regioisomers.
